subject: physics_2
question_text: Write the colour code of a carbon resistor of resistance 350 mΩ ± 10%.

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Transcription: the book (p28, VSAQ 21) prints 350mΩ ± 10% without a space before the unit; a space is inserted. Note this is a DIFFERENT question from VSAQ 9 (p27), which asks for 350 MΩ with 5% tolerance — milli-ohm here, mega-ohm there. Hand-checked: 350 mΩ = 350 × 10⁻³ Ω = 35 × 10⁻² Ω, so digits 3 and 5 with multiplier 10⁻², giving Orange, Green, Silver, and Silver for ±10% — the same four colours the book prints.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Two digits and a multiplier
lines: The colour code carries two significant
digits, then a power-of-ten multiplier, then
steps.margin_note: First mark. Rewrite the value as two digits times a power of ten.
steps.why: The first two bands can only show two digits, so the value has to be written as a two-digit number times a power of ten before any colour can be read off.
common_mistakes: Leaving it as 350 × 10⁻³. Three digits cannot be shown on two bands.
Reading mΩ as MΩ. Small m is milli, 10⁻³.

recall.must_convey: That 350 milli-ohm is written as 35 times ten to the power minus two ohm.

steps.memory_tip: Two digits first: turn 350 into 35 and move the rest into the power of ten.

steps.label: The four colours
steps.margin_note: Second mark. All four bands in order, including the tolerance band.
steps.why: Gold and Silver do double duty in this code: as multipliers they mean 10⁻¹ and 10⁻², and as tolerance bands they mean ±5% and ±10%. Here Silver appears in both roles.
common_mistakes: Giving only three bands. The tolerance band is asked for as well.
Using Gold for 10⁻². Gold is 10⁻¹; Silver is 10⁻².

recall.must_convey: That the bands are Orange, Green, Silver and Silver.
accept: three is orange five is green
silver for ten power minus two and silver for ten percent

steps.memory_tip: Silver twice: once as the multiplier 10⁻², once as the ±10% band.

insider_note: Silver is both the multiplier band and the tolerance band here. Students who write only three colours lose the second mark.
